Holding the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% while continuing QT keeps policy restrictively biased even as inflation eases. In New Keynesian, forecast-based frameworks (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), this pause acknowledges transmission lags and data dependence, but the explicit readiness for “additional policy firming” and persistence of balance-sheet runoff mean financial conditions remain tight. Consistent with Bernanke–Mihov’s identification of policy stance via reserve dynamics, non-rate tools (QT, IORB/ON RRP in the floor system adopted post-2008) can maintain restraint without a hike. The communication strategy aligns with Romer and Romer’s narrative emphasis: guard against upside inflation risks while observing cooling growth and a still-strong labor market. Net tone: slightly negative.
